title: Effect set · Four surfaces
premise: Two stocks and two marks, one material system. Paper and cloth are height fields; pen dots and a roller print into them through one ink chain; one sheet light rakes all of it. No gradient stands in for anything.
source: Mindgut · Technique & Front-End Study V01 §08 (texture recipes) · ø co. · 2026-10-23

system.read: Ink on real stock under one raking light.
sharedCause: stock height field → relief shading · ink acceptance · starved pinholes · wicking · ink mottle
sheet light → paper relief · thread modeling · thread cast shadows · object shadows on the page
passOrder: stock height (tooth · fibers · pits · formation | threads)
albedo (paper L, thread dyes in OKLab)
ink pressure (dot footprints | roller run-out) × mask
acceptance vs height → starve → wick → film thickness
color: Beer–Lambert film in linear light (or coverage mix)
light: × Lambert shade × height shadow (once, last)

light.note: az = direction the light comes FROM (screen degrees, 0 = right, 90 = below); el = elevation above the sheet; one light for every plate, usage and shadow

units: CSS px for every length; rendered at device px (dpr ≤ 2). Density params change mark count per px², never a tile scale.

shared.blueNoise: 64 × 64 void-and-cluster rank tile, σ 1.9, toroidal, seed 1993
shared.mask: signed distance to rect | ellipse | band | blob, displaced by fbm (wander, scale, octaves), feather as tone or blue-noise speckle, bite = clumped dropouts rising toward the edge; cached by params

effects.name: Stipple ramp
effects.sub: Tone made of whole pen dots pressed into the stock. Value sets how many sites print (FM) or how big each dot is (AM); a blue-noise rank picks the sites; each dot's rim loses pressure, so the stock's tooth decides how ragged it prints.
recipe: Site lattice at the pitch (CSS px), jittered. Value field (linear · radial · noise) eased from → to.
Screen: FM keeps a site when its blue-noise rank < value; AM keeps every site with radius ∝ √value; the dial interpolates. The mask is sampled at the site — dots are whole or absent.
Each dot is a pressure footprint: 7 vertex radii (irregular nib), peak = pen pressure, falling to 0 across the nib-softness rim.
Ink chain: pressure against the stock height → acceptance (peaks first), starved valleys, wick along fibers, film thickness τ.
Color: Beer–Lambert film in linear light (or a coverage mix). Ink B overprints by the same film product.
Light last: × the stock's shading under the sheet light.

limits.what: sites merge into flat tone at 1× — the stipple stops reading as marks
dots fuse into a solid; FM loses its range
dots print as broken rings — the stock shows through every one
clumps and voids at low density

effects.name: Ink leaving paper
effects.sub: A solid that runs out. Roller pressure eases off across a warped edge; as it falls, only the peaks of the stock still touch the ink, so the run-out speckle is the paper's own tooth — with pinholes in its valleys and hairlines wicked along its fibers.
recipe: Pressure = dropoff curve of the signed distance to a warped edge line (stroke direction, transition width), × the mask.

Ink chain: the stock height under the inked area (blended with film-splitting noise, clumped and streaked along the stroke) is ranked to percentiles; pressure P inks exactly the top P of the surface — peaks first.
Starve: valleys below the threshold never take ink. Wick: fibers carry ink past the edge. Mottle: paper formation thins the film.
Film thickness thins with pressure unless the film breaks up; color = Beer–Lambert film in linear light.
Light last: × the stock's shading — the ink sits in the tooth, not on top of it.

limits.what: reads as a hard vector edge — no run-out to see
the edge becomes a gradient — the "AI gradient" failure
speckle stops following the paper — reads as digital dither
marks read as scanlines unless the angle is off-axis

effects.name: Paper tooth
effects.sub: White stock that is not a screen. A height field — tooth, formation, laid fibers, pits — lit by the one sheet light. On white the relief can only take light away, so the paper reads through its shadows. FX-01 and FX-02 print into this exact field.
recipe: Height = fbm at the tooth scale (octaves, persistence = how fast detail drops off), reshaped by the distribution curve; blended with low-frequency formation.
Fibers: curved capsules at a count per 100 × 100 px near the grain angle, raised into the height; pits: small depressions. Both also darken the albedo slightly.
Normal from the height gradient → Lambert under the sheet light (azimuth + elevation from the light puck). Diffuse share vs ambient fill; the fill can be tinted.
The same field is the stock for FX-01 and FX-02: its peaks take ink first, its valleys starve, its fibers wick.
Mask = the sheet's cut or deckle edge; the sheet casts a contact + ambient shadow onto the page by the same light.

limits.what: reads as stucco or dirt, not stock
collapses into per-pixel noise — digital grain
every fiber becomes a hard ridge; ok for a raking-light study, not for a page

effects.name: Weave
effects.sub: Cloth built as cloth: warp and weft at their own counts, a real interlacing, slubbed and hairy threads, every float a raised body lit by the sheet light and casting into the gaps. A cut edge frays thread by thread. FX-01 and FX-02 can print onto it.
recipe: Warp columns and weft rows at their own counts (threads / 100 CSS px); each thread: jittered center, thickness, dye-lot L, fray length, accent.

Interlacing decides the top thread per crossing; a float is the run where it stays on top. Height = cylinder across the thread × arch along the float; under-threads sit low; hair = fine noise along the thread.
Albedo in OKLab: under-thread, then top thread by AA coverage; accent as flecks (single floats, as in the source) or whole threads.
Light: Lambert from the height gradient + a height-field shadow march toward the sheet light, so floats shade into the gaps; ambient occlusion darkens the gaps.
Cut: the mask's signed distance plus each thread's own fray length — threads end raggedly, not on a line. The swatch casts onto the page.

limits.what: threads under 2.5 px alias against the display — moiré
reads as a grid of strokes, not cloth
gutters close; the weave flattens to a check

usages.title: Meter · counted marks
usages.sub: Three readings as stipple printed into paper. Value is the share of the bar that prints; the bar's end runs out by the dropoff curve, and the dots there print broken because pressure — not just count — falls.

usages.title: Ticket · two runs on one stock
usages.sub: A die-cut ticket on the page: a roller band that runs out before the stub, then the text as a second run of black through the same chain — full pressure, so only the paper's deepest valleys starve it. Perforation and shadow by the sheet light.

usages.title: Swatch · frayed linen on the page
usages.sub: The weave cut by a blob mask: every thread ends at its own length, the swatch lifts off the page and casts by the sheet light. Natural linen dyes; same functions as the dark source plate.

usages.title: Headline · ink runs out of the word
usages.sub: Type rasterized as a pressure clip; the roller crosses it and runs out, so the last letters print on the paper's peaks only. Type is a mask in the press layer, never a gradient fill.

usages.title: Overprint · two inks, one film
usages.sub: Two stipple ramps crossing inside an ellipse. Where dots overlap, Beer–Lambert multiplies the films into a third color; switch the color rule on FX-01 to compare coverage mixes.

usages.title: Screenprint · ink on linen
usages.sub: The roller from FX-02 printed onto the cloth stock instead of paper: ink catches the top floats first, misses the gaps and the low under-threads, and the weave's light still models it.
